public_payload.normalized_proposition: GenAI systems fail to understand simple concepts such as designing for one-handed use.

statement.excerpt: They fail to “understand” simple concepts, such as “design to used with only one hand.”

from_speaker: design to used with only one hand
Noncanonical situations continue to remain difficult
Attracted to does not of course mean that no other output is possible
our_interpretation: Read in context, this concerns contemporary image generators repeatedly failing to translate simple requirements into suitable designs. It does not say every output fails.
Treat understanding operationally: whether generated designs satisfy the requested requirement. This cannot establish the presence or absence of an internal mental state.
Ordinary prompts may state the functional requirement without specifying the complete solution. Occasional success, especially with detailed instructions, is compatible with the claim.

The target is capability as of February 8, 2024. Earlier tests of the contemporary systems are eligible. No common starting date is supplied, so the lower date boundary is left unspecified rather than imposing a one-week window.
criteria.support_condition: Documented, reproducible tests of contemporary image generators show recurring failures to satisfy simple functional design requirements, including one-handed operation or closely comparable constraints, with ordinary prompts and disclosed outputs.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable tests show that contemporary image generators reliably satisfy those requirements across ordinary prompt variations and repeated outputs. A selected successful image alone is insufficient.

DEsignBench provides a contemporary comparison of image generators in design scenarios. Expanded prompts and visual-design evaluation do not directly settle compliance with an ordinary request for one-handed operation.
